title: Not a Father's Day
cn: 第 7 集 · 非父亲节
novel:
Marshall and Lily [[panicked|panic]]. They thought Lily might be [[pregnant|pregnant]], and they were not ready. Marshall [[agonized|agonize]] over the responsibility. Lily [[doubted|doubt]] her own [[maturity|maturity]].

"Are we ready for this?" Marshall asked, pacing the room.

"I don't know," Lily [[whispered|whisper]].

The test was [[negative|negative]]. Relief and [[disappointment|disappointment]] mixed together in a confusing wave. They realized they needed more time to [[prepare|prepare]].

Meanwhile, Barney [[invented|invent]] a holiday called "Not a Father's Day." He [[celebrated|celebrate]] the freedom of men without children. He bought [[t-shirts|t-shirt]] that read "No Kids" and threw a wild party.

"This is [[liberating|liberate]]," Barney [[declared|declare]]. "No [[diapers|diaper]], no [[screaming|scream]] babies, no [[sacrifices|sacrifice]]."

Marshall went to Barney's party and tried to enjoy the freedom. But he could not stop thinking about having a family someday. "I want kids," he [[admitted|admit]] to Barney.

Barney [[scoffed|scoff]]. "You're [[insane|insane]]."

But later that night, Barney held a tiny [[t-shirt|t-shirt]] he had bought as a joke. He stared at it for a long time. Something [[stirred|stir]] inside him — a feeling he would never [[admit|admit]] to anyone.

Marshall went home and held Lily's hand. "When the time is right," he said.

She nodded. "We'll know."

agonize.en: to spend a long time worrying

doubt.en: to not feel certain about something

maturity.en: the quality of being fully grown in mind

negative.en: showing that something is not present

disappointment.en: the sad feeling when something is not as good as hoped

invent.en: to make or think of something new

celebrate.en: to do something enjoyable for a special day

t-shirt.en: a simple cotton shirt with short sleeves

diaper.en: a piece of cloth for a baby's bottom

scream.en: to make a loud high cry

sacrifice.en: giving up something important for someone else

admit.en: to agree that something is true

scoff.en: to laugh at something in a rude way

stir.en: to cause a feeling to begin
